title: Power of Four
prompt: Given an integer `n`, return `true` if it is a power of four, meaning `n` can be written as `4^x` for some non-negative integer `x`. Otherwise return `false`.
hints: Every power of four is also a power of two, so start by checking that n has exactly one bit set.
Not every power of two is a power of four — 8 is a power of two but not four. What distinguishes them is which bit position is set.
Powers of four have their single set bit at an even position (0, 2, 4, ...). Use a mask like 0x55555555 (bits at even positions) and check that ANDing it with n reproduces n itself.

solution.approach: First confirm n is positive and a power of two using n & (n - 1) == 0. Among powers of two, powers of four are exactly those whose single set bit sits at an even index (positions 0, 2, 4, ...), since 4^x = 2^(2x). Checking n & 0x55555555 == n verifies the set bit lies only among the even-indexed positions (0x55555555 has 1s at every even bit of a 32-bit number).
